requirement:
When replacing results for an unfiltered workspace invocation or a filtered
invocation selecting at least one test, a prepared build configuration
incompatible with the active configuration under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` clears the whole
current set and becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before test
execution.

Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that
configuration is selected again. A filtered invocation selecting no tests
leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration_reset` states only observable behavior, so it has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. There are no review roots or acknowledgments, and I did not read any source code.

I checked each clause for a structural obligation and found none:
- "clears the whole current set and becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before test execution": This says what the stored state is after a replacement and when it changes. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegated interface. A different design could still show the same behavior. For example, it could write a new database and swap it in, or run one transaction. Such a design would still clear the old set, activate the new configuration, and finish both before any test starts. So the choice of mechanism is discretionary.
- "Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that configuration is selected again": This is observable behavior.
- "A filtered invocation selecting no tests leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged": This is observable behavior. The text defers it to `requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`, which the requirement cites for context.

The cited `requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` and `requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace` supply context only. They define what counts as an incompatible build configuration and how a replacement is atomic. Both are also stated as behavior.

behavioral: **Obligations and the tests that cover them**

1. **A filtered invocation selecting at least one test, with an incompatible configuration, clears the whole set and activates the new configuration.**
   - `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[incompatible_builds_reset_every_test_but_empty_focused_runs_do_not]` first stores two tests under configuration "a" and completes one of them.
   - It then replaces with a filtered run (`true`) under "b" that selects one test.
   - It asserts the configuration is "b" and only one test remains. That test is pending with no measurements, so the unselected test and the old measurement were cleared.

2. **An unfiltered invocation with an incompatible configuration clears the whole set and activates the new configuration.**
   - The same test completes two tests under "a", then runs an unfiltered replace (`false`) under "b" that selects one test.
   - It asserts the configuration is "b" and one test remains. That test is `a` and is pending with no measurements.

3. **Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that configuration is selected again.**
   - The same test switches back to "a" with a filtered run selecting only `b`.
   - It asserts exactly one test remains, `b`, with no measurements.
   - If the earlier "a" result or the unselected test had been preserved or restored, the count or identity would differ.

4. **A filtered invocation selecting no tests leaves the results and active configuration unchanged.**
   - The same test calls `replace(&empty, &[], true)` under the different configuration "b".
   - It asserts the call returns false.
   - It then asserts the configuration is still "a", both tests remain, the measurements are retained, and the latest invocation is the empty run's id.
   - This is the `storage.replace` behaviour that the requirement cites.

5. **The clear and the activation happen in the same atomic replacement, before test execution.**
   - `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[failed_atomic_replacement_preserves_results_configuration_and_invocation]` forces a failure of an incompatible-configuration ("b") replacement with a trigger on `tests` insert.
   - It asserts the configuration, latest invocation, test id and measurements all stay as before. So the clear and the configuration switch are not partially applied.
   - `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[a_failed_replacement_commit_reports_the_error_without_launching_execution]` does the same end to end after a configuration change (`--features alpha`).
   - It asserts the command fails and reports the error, and that no nextest execution starts. It also asserts the stored runs and measurements are unchanged.
   - The no-execution assertion supports the "before test execution" ordering.

The determination of which configurations are incompatible belongs to `requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`, which this requirement only cites. I did not reassess it.

I found no untested behavioural obligation and no marking gap. All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

text: :::{req} storage.configuration_reset
When replacing results for an unfiltered workspace invocation or a filtered
invocation selecting at least one test, a prepared build configuration
incompatible with the active configuration under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` clears the whole
current set and becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before test
execution.
Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that
configuration is selected again. A filtered invocation selecting no tests
leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`.
:::{req} storage.configuration
Each coverage record MUST identify the recorded toolchain, compilation target,
Cargo build profile, enabled features, and instrumentation-affecting compiler
settings. These settings MUST determine build-configuration compatibility for
the combined view. A nextest scheduling profile alone MUST NOT make otherwise
compatible build configurations incompatible.
:::{req} storage.replace
After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected
test starts, Habeas atomically establishes the new coverage set:
- An unfiltered workspace invocation clears the entire previous set,
including results for tests that no longer exist. This includes
`habeas coverage` with no supplied arguments and `habeas test`.
- An invocation with an explicit package or binary restriction, test filter,
partition, or ignored-only selection is filtered. It clears results for all
selected test identities and preserves unselected results within the
active build configuration.
- Every selected test receives a pending entry without measurements.
Native default filters and the default handling of ignored tests still apply
to an unfiltered workspace invocation. `--run-ignored all` alone does not make
a workspace invocation filtered.
A selected test that never starts because of fail-fast, interruption, or
execution startup failure remains unavailable. Its previous result does not
become available again. A filtered selection containing no tests leaves the
current results and active configuration unchanged; an empty unfiltered
workspace selection clears the previous set.
If the atomic replacement cannot be committed, the command reports the
failure and starts no tests. The previously committed coverage set and active
configuration remain unchanged.
